decision: ran the checker with the omarky extract as the reference list
why: proves no extracted behaviour was lost in adaptation

decision: spot-checked adapted items in page, writer, reader and keymap by reading them
why: agent summaries are not evidence
evidence: behavior/page-and-typography.md PAGE-21 PAGE-25 PAGE-87, writer.md WR-01 to WR-05 WR-225, keymap.md conflict table

decision: commit omarky extracts under source/omarky-0.7.0 and point check-specs coverage at them

result: 664 items, exit 0, every extract ID present

decision: roadmap in README.md: nine phases, harness first, Rune patch spike second, writer after reader
why: riskiest unknown (Rune patch, typing latency) must be proven before writer work builds on it
result: phase list written; no code yet

decision: deferred work in TODO.md: changes mode, Claude rewrite, spelling, user keymap file

decision: phase 1 and phase 2 run at once in separate checkouts: harness on branch rw/phase-1-harness in Quire, Rune patch in a separate clone at ~/Projects/rune-quire
why: they touch different code; the user forbids worktrees, so the seam is a separate repo, not a second checkout of Quire

decision: omarky references rendered by a third agent into the scratchpad only
why: keeps git writes to one agent per checkout; omarky repo left untouched

decision: Rune patch on fable, harness on opus, omarky renders on sonnet
why: the patch is the hardest change (text layout internals); the renders are mechanical

decision: agents limited to one cargo build at a time, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, agents slice capped
why: two parallel builds ran the laptop out of memory and the user asked for limits

decision: phases 1 (harness) and 2 (Rune paragraph patch) paused, work parked on rw/phase-1-harness and in ~/Projects/rune-quire
why: the user said to skip them and build features
evidence: user: "Skip this stage, you are just wasting time"
result: decision 0004 stays open; verification is unit tests plus headless --snap renders until the harness returns

decision: debug builds compile dependencies at opt-level 1 without debug info, and the agents' memory cap went from 4 GB to 8 GB
why: under 4 GB the build spent 94% of its CPU time reclaiming memory and never finished
evidence: cgroup cpu.stat: system 94,610 s vs user 6,746 s

decision: bold iA faces registered with OS/2 weight 700, patched in memory
why: Quattro S Bold ships declaring weight 400, so bold runs matched Regular; the OFL Reserved Font Name forbids changing the files
evidence: fontTools read of the shipped files; test page_02

decision: zoom follows omarky's ladder round(14.4 z), 9 to 32 px, Ctrl+=/-/0
why: PAGE-19

decision: colour roles mix per sRGB channel, not with Rune's linear-light Color::mix
why: omarky mixes as Qt and CSS do; linear mixing gives visibly lighter greys
evidence: test page_34 (#000 to #fff at 0.4 is #666666, not #aaaaaa)
result: verified on Paper and Nord renders

decision: built-in themes take named colours from Omarchy's own theme files where Omarchy ships the theme, else the published palette; Paper, White, Ink and Black have none and fall back to the accent
why: code then looks as it does in omarky under the matching Omarchy theme
result: open: Paper code will be accent-only until someone picks named colours for it

decision: the keymap table stores chords in the spec's notation and a test reads keymap.md to compare every KEY item
why: keeps the spec and the code from drifting

decision: actions without a handler fall through and are hidden from Settings, Shortcuts
why: reader and writer keys arrive with their phases; listing dead keys would mislead
result: default preset omarky moves the palette to Ctrl+Shift+K and the mode switch to Ctrl+P

decision: highlighter crate choice moved to phase 5
why: nothing renders highlighted code before the reader page; the style table (PAGE-50) is ready

decision: reduced motion is Rune's per-commit override fed by QUIRE_REDUCED_MOTION, Hyprland animations:enabled and the system setting, plus motion::ms for Quire's own durations
why: Rune already snaps springs, flights and glides under the override

decision: both side panels take omarky outline type, spacing and text colours (decision 0008)
why: user asked for omarky sidebar fonts and spacing; RD-42 to RD-50 already specify the outline
evidence: ui/panel.rs, tests rd_45 rd_46, snaps light and dark
result: verified by snapshot and unit test; hover colour transition (120 ms) not animated

decision: panel font is the family fc-match monospace names, not Family::SystemMono
why: Rune loads only the regular face for SystemMono, so bold rendered regular

decision: parser is pulldown-cmark 0.13 (no default features) with tables, GFM footnotes, strikethrough, smart punctuation and wiki links; markdown-it's extras (typographer replacements, linkify, tags) run over its text runs
why: it gives byte ranges for every event, which become the line maps; extending md.rs meant writing a CommonMark parser; comrak is larger for the same result
evidence: blocks.rs, 35 tests ported from omarky's tst_blocks plus extras

decision: no architect run for the parser choice
why: only one crate met the line-map need at small size; the block model's shape was already fixed by omarky's tst_blocks tables

decision: a paragraph of two or more images becomes a gallery; ![[file.png|300]] becomes an embedded image, ![[Note]] a wiki link
why: Quire notes write image rows and Obsidian embeds, which omarky does not read

decision: single-tilde ~x~ strikes in Quire but not in omarky
why: pulldown-cmark's strikethrough takes one or two tildes; markdown-it takes two

decision: preview draws every block kind from blocks::build; the old md::blocks, md::toggle_task and image_line are deleted; task boxes set a state rather than flip one
why: one model for the reader; the box writes the state the reader saw
result: verified by snapshot: every kind draws; styling of alerts, footnote marks and tables left to phase 5

decision: code colours come from rune-highlights (Rune's own lexers, same rev as rune); Zed capture names map onto the KSyntax styles of roles.rs; omarky's aliases (sh, shell, console, tex, math, jsonc, patch) apply first
why: it ships with Rune, needs no grammar files, and its token names map one to one onto the styles phase 3 built; syntect would bring a second theme system
result: verified by unit test and snapshot

decision: Paper, White, Ink and Black carry named colours (light: muted green #5f7a3a, red #b0432f, yellow #a2741b, blue #3d6a9c; dark: lighter versions); the other themes keep their upstream palettes
why: resolves the open question: without them every code colour and the diff bands fell back to the accent
evidence: roles test page_41 (paper has its own; a theme without falls back), kitchen-sink snapshot
result: verified: diff bands green and red on Paper

decision: page geometry (measure, gutter, lean, rhythm table, table widths) is pure functions in page.rs, drawn by preview.rs
why: the numbers are the spec; testing them apart from layout is cheap
evidence: page.rs tests page_13_14_15, page_21_to_27, page_54_to_65, page_66_67, blk_63_to_65

decision: octicons are drawn from the JetBrainsMono Nerd Font's octicon glyphs, extracted to SVG paths
why: same shapes as omarky's GitHub icons with no new asset licence

decision: footnote references use the font's superscript digits rather than a raised baseline
why: Rune spans have no baseline shift; iA Quattro has the superscript digits

decision: the crumb stays above the page, with the 44 px top room below it; the "full" width setting maps to the wide measure
why: Quire shows the file path in the reader; omarky has no third width

decision: deferred: virtualization for long notes, code and table edge fades, the task box's hover border, inline chip borders, hover colour transitions, the heading # and copy chips (phase 6)
why: none blocks reading; fades and hover need Rune work or belong with phase 6's behaviour
